text.p: Italian bond futures started on the lower track as the market paused for breath after this week's sharp rally in prices, but dealers said the outlook still remained generally positive for the BTP market.

They added that futures had become technically overbought after strong rises on Monday and Tuesday while the slight weakness of the lira and dollar against the German mark added to the early market weakness.
"The trend, however, is still bullish as the market looks towards a fall in Italian inflation and interest rates," said one trader on the LIFFE market in London.

Dealers said that the market was heartened by an expected fall in April's preliminary CPI next week which is set to see annual CPI dip below two percent and this could spark a cut in Italian interest rates before the end of the month.

The market received further support late Tuesday as U.S. March CPI data showed a benign 0.1 percent rise and so eased pressures on the U.S. Federal Reserve to tighten interest rates further, thus pushed U.S. T-bonds sharply higher.
"The mood on the BTPs is postive with the only concern at the moment being watching the lira-mark cross rate," the LIFFE trader said.

Dealers said data showing Italian February producer prices rising an annual 0.8 percent after January's 0.9 percent year-on-year rise, and wholesale inflation up 0.5 percent in Feb after a 1.0 percent rise in Jan had little immediate impact.
